sections.h2: What does the Jefferson County Recorder do from 301 Market Street?
sections.html:
The Recorder in Steubenville makes the permanent record of every paper that moves land, places a mortgage or adds another charge on it in Jefferson County. The address is 301 Market Street, Steubenville, OH 43952, and a statewide legal aid directory lists weekday hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Ask the office for its current fee schedule before you go.

Jefferson County hugs the Ohio River along the West Virginia line, and Steubenville is both the seat and the largest city. The Recorder takes deeds for every parcel in the county, including those in Toronto, the only other city, and in the villages and townships between. Property across the river in Brooke or Hancock County, West Virginia, falls under West Virginia's own recording system.

sections.h2: How does Ohio build the Jefferson County recording fee?
sections.html:
R.C. 317.32 sets each charge as a base fee with a matching Ohio housing trust fund fee. Ask the Recorder for the total on your paper before you write the check. The statute's components are:

  • the first two pages: $17 base plus $17 housing trust fund
  • each added page of 8.5 by 14 inches or part of one: $4 base plus $4 housing trust fund
  • each marginal reference made by a separate instrument: $2 plus $2
  • a certified copy: $1 plus $1 per page, with another 50 cents plus 50 cents when the recorder's seal is needed
  • an optional document preservation surcharge of up to $5, credited to the county general fund

Senate Bill 94 added the preservation surcharge, effective October 24, 2024. Whether Jefferson County applies it, and at what amount below the cap, is a question for the Recorder.

sections.h2: What conveyance charges come due when a Jefferson County house sells?
sections.html:
The Auditor collects two layers before the deed goes to the Recorder. The state layer is in R.C. 319.54(G)(3): one dollar, or ten cents per hundred dollars or fraction of value, whichever is greater. The local layer is the county's optional real property transfer tax under R.C. 322.02, which cannot exceed thirty cents per hundred dollars.

The county's 2025 annual financial report speaks of a four mill permissive conveyance fee and says the commissioners dedicated one mill of it to the GIS Fund. The Auditor is at 301 Market Street, P.O. Box 159, Steubenville, with phone (740) 283-8511 and fax (740) 283-8520. Confirm the rate in force with that office, because commissioners set a permissive levy by resolution.

The seller bears the cost (R.C. 319.202(D)). When a transfer is exempt, the deed carries a statement giving the reason for the exemption in place of the fee.

sections.h2: Which Jefferson County transfers escape the conveyance fee?
sections.html:
R.C. 319.54(G)(3) lists about two dozen exempt transfers. The ones most likely to matter for a family house in Steubenville or one of the townships are:

  • a gift from one spouse to another, or between a parent and child or the spouse of either
  • a transfer among the heirs or devisees of one decedent when no money changes hands
  • a deed to the trustee of a trust whose maker kept an unlimited power to revoke
  • a deed confirming or correcting a deed already recorded
  • a transfer valued at one hundred dollars or less
  • a court-ordered transfer, unless it results from a sale made under the order

An investor purchase is a different case. A quick as-is sale to a cash buyer is still a fee-paying transfer, and the cost comes out of the seller's side of the closing.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Jefferson County homes?
sections.html:
QuickFacts shows 30,964 housing units for July 2025 and a 70.5% owner-occupied rate. For 2020 to 2024 the median owner-occupied home is valued at $127,800, median gross rent is $835 and median household income is $59,055. People 65 and older are 23.9% of residents, a larger share than in Holmes, Huron or Jackson counties, and 17.7% live in poverty.

Population slid 2.5% between the April 2020 base and July 2025, the steepest drop of the four. The Weirton-Steubenville metropolitan area, which adds Brooke and Hancock counties in West Virginia, is the labor market most residents work in.

sections.h2: How does the Auditor step fit with recording in Jefferson County?
sections.html:
The Auditor goes first. R.C. 322.02 requires any county transfer tax to be paid by the grantor to the auditor when the deed is delivered, and before it is presented to the recorder. The Auditor endorses the deed with the fee amount, and the endorsed deed then goes to the Recorder.

R.C. 317.13 told every Ohio recorder, auditor and engineer to offer an electronic way of recording conveyance papers by June 30, 2026, and that date has passed. A Steubenville title company can file a closing package electronically instead of carrying it across the floor. A seller handling a deed alone should bring the signed, notarized original if the office wants paper.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Steubenville and the county?
sections.html:
The United States built Fort Steuben in 1786 to protect surveyors mapping land west of the Ohio River. Settlers built homes around it, calling the place La Belle at first, and the town was later renamed Steubenville for the fort. Jefferson County was organized on July 29, 1797, six years before Ohio became a state, and took its present shape in 1833 after Carroll County was formed.

Ohio Route 7 is the main north-south highway, and Pittsburgh International Airport is reachable to the east by U.S. Route 22. The county has about 408 square miles of land, with Columbiana, Belmont, Carroll and Harrison counties and West Virginia along its edges.

faqs.q: Where is a deed for a Steubenville house recorded?
faqs.a: At the Jefferson County Recorder, 301 Market Street, Steubenville. A deed is recorded in the county that holds the land, and Steubenville lies in Jefferson County.

faqs.q: Does Jefferson County charge the optional document preservation surcharge?
faqs.a: Ask the Recorder. R.C. 317.32 allows a surcharge of up to five dollars, and the office can tell you what it adds to a deed.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance fee on a Jefferson County sale?
faqs.a: The seller. R.C. 319.202(D) charges the grantor with the Auditor's fee under R.C. 319.54(G)(3) and any transfer tax the county has levied under Chapter 322.

faqs.q: Is a gift from a parent to a child exempt from the conveyance fee in Jefferson County?
faqs.a: Yes, under R.C. 319.54(G)(3)(d), which covers a gift between a parent and child or the spouse of either. The deed still goes to the Auditor with an exemption statement before it is recorded.

faqs.q: What is the four mill fee in the Jefferson County financial report?
faqs.a: It is the county's permissive conveyance fee. The 2025 report says the commissioners dedicated one mill of the four mill fee to the county's GIS Fund, which keeps the parcel maps current.
